<thought>From the 13C NMR data, there are 18 carbon signals. The signals at 166.40 ppm and 52.24 ppm correspond to a carbonyl carbon and an aliphatic carbon, respectively, and are not aromatic. All remaining signals (from 142.60 ppm down to 125.50 ppm) fall in the typical aromatic carbon region, including duplicate peaks that represent distinct aromatic carbons. Therefore, the number of aromatic carbon atoms is 18 − 2 = 16.</thought>
<final_answer>16</final_answer>
